title: Monotonicity of the number of functions determined by additive relations
statement:
Let $E$ be a set and $S$ a set of arithmetic functions. For positive integers $k$ and $ell$, let $n(E,S,k)$ denote the number of functions in $S$ determined by the relation

$$
f(a_1+a_2+\dotsb+a_k)=f(a_1)+f(a_2)+\dotsb+f(a_k)
$$

for arbitrary $a_i\in E$. **The monotonicity conjecture for $n(E,S,k)$.** If $E$ and $S$ determine $n(E,S,k)$ in this way, then

$$
n(E,S,k)\ge n(E,S,\ell)
$$

when $k\le \ell$. The paper describes this as a generalization of the preceding conjecture, and gives no resolution.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.00897

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).
source_name: Poo-Sung Park, “k-additive uniqueness of the set of squares for multiplicative functions”, arXiv:1612.00897 (2016).
